newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarians pay respect to murdered ex-premier.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarians pay respect to murdered ex-premier.

text.p: Thousands of Bulgarians queued on Friday to pay their respects to Andrei Lukanov, as a colleague said the former prime minister had been about to expose high-level corruption when he was murdered.

President Zhelyu Zhelev and Prime Minister Zhan Videnov led members of the cabinet, politicians, diplomats and Bulgaria's Eastern Orthodox Patriarch Maxim in filing past the flower-covered coffin in parliament's Saint Sofia hall.
Moscow-educated Lukanov, 58, a millionaire businessman and member of parliament for the ruling Socialists, was found shot dead in front of his Sofia home on Wednesday.

State radio said a forensic examination showed Lukanov was killed with three bullets in the back and one in the head. Investigators declined to speculate on the motive for the killing, the radio added.
But Socialist Party colleague Andrei Raichev told the Standard Daily on Friday that the murder had prevented Lukanov from disclosing corruption in top government circles.
"A day before his murder Lukanov told me: "I have clear proof of corruption at the highest levels of power and I plan to take real steps'," he said.
Raichev, a leader of the party's reform wing, said Lukanov had postponed a trip to the United States to pursue the matter.
Raichev said this was a strong motive for the killing. The murder was also aimed at frightening people in a position to act against this corruption, he added.
Raichev said Lukanov intended to take on the Socialist Party's current leaders. "He thought they were not only corrupted, but they were very bad at governing the state."
Both president Zhelev and prime minister Videnov praised the dead man, who was one of the architects of the downfall of communist dictator Todor Zhivkov in 1989.
"We are losing a prominent statesman, a bright cadre of the democratic Left and an active participant in the democratic changes in the country," Videnov said.
Zhelev described Lukanov as a key figure in Bulgaria's post-communist history.
"The actions and the personality of Andrei Lukanov were as contradictory as the (country's) transition period is. He became a victim of the actions which he had started," he said
Earlier this year Lukanov accused the Socialist Party of reviving the functions of the Stalinist state and restoring ties with the secret services.
A friend of Russia's Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, he was one of the founders of a Bulgarian-Russian gas joint stock company, Topenergy.
Politicians said this role troubled his relations with Videnov. In July Lukanov was dropped as Topenergy's chairman.

He served as prime minister for six months in 1990 but resigned due to widespread public dissatisfaction with the sluggish pace of reform. Under his rule, Bulgaria declared a moratorium on $12 billion of foreign debt.

In 1992 the public prosecutor launched an inquiry into whether Lukanov had misappropriated funds in the 1980s when he was a deputy prime minister. He was stripped of parliamentary rights and detained for six months until the case was dropped.
Lukanov was being buried later on Friday in a family tomb in Sofia by family and close friends.

Foreign guests at the funeral included Yugoslavia's Deputy Prime Minister Uros Klikovac, Greek Decentralisation Minister Alexandros Papadopoulos and Turkish Ministers of State Bekir Aksoy and Ahmet Cemil Tunc.
The long line of waiting mourners stretched round the corner of the parliament building.
